title: Delhi HC Confirms Injunction Against Jabsons Foods Over 'HOT MIX' Namkeen Mark
case_name: Sunit Shah, Proprietor, M/s Shah Namkeen v. M/s Jabsons Foods Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: The Delhi High Court confirmed its interim injunction restraining Jabsons Foods from using 'HOT MIX' for namkeen, dismissing its plea to vacate the order. Adding the house mark 'JABSONS' and varying the packaging did not cure the infringement, since 'HOT MIX', the dominant feature of Shah Namkeen's registered 'SHAH HOT MIX' label, was reproduced in full. Other traders' similar use elsewhere was no defence here.
card_tip: A house mark added alongside a reproduced dominant feature does not defeat infringement, and a defendant cannot rely on third parties' unrelated use of a similar mark to excuse its own.
verification_notes: Confirmed by three independent reports (LiveLawBiz, Verdictum, Asia IP Law) agreeing on parties, citation, date and holding; judgment itself not accessed. Note a separate 2024 District Court ruling involving a different defendant (BC HOT MIX) reached the opposite result on different facts; not inconsistent with this order.
